brief.headline: Push for ₹28.69 L/yr in savings to match our best prices — you're nearly half their business, so they need you more than you need them

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the prices Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic give us on the same items
priceAsk.target: ₹28.69 L/yr in savings by closing the gap to our best prices
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars Plastics ₹0.81/NOS for the 28mm PP cap that Cincorp charges ₹1.08 (33.2% more), and Premier Plastic charges ₹0.35/NOS for the measuring cup that Cincorp charges ₹0.46 (30.6% more). The market asking price for the 28mm cap is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, so our Mars price of ₹0.81 is even sharper — Cincorp should match it or come very close.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 45 days — they already take 39 days to pay their own suppliers (versus 23 days for similar firms), so asking for more would squeeze them unfairly

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is a small maker (₹4.11 Cr in sales) and we're 47.43% of their revenue — losing us would cut them nearly in half. They keep only 6.0% of every ₹100 they sell, far less than similar firms (15.0%), so their margins are already thin. They owe 1.13 times their own cash and their financial health sits at C (51/100) in the grey zone, meaning they're stable today but not strong. Because we're such a big customer and they're tight on profit, push hard on price but don't over-squeeze — we need them to stay in business and deliver on time.

evidence.point: They keep far less profit than rivals
We're paying ₹28.69 L/yr more than our cheapest supplier for the same sort of items
On the 28mm PP cap, we pay Cincorp 33.2% more than Mars Plastics
They take longer to pay their own suppliers than similar firms do
They owe more than their own cash

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's biggest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr) with pharma bottles, caps and preforms — a proven, healthy (B 65/100) second source already on our list

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed leader in rigid plastics for pharma (₹1010.97 Cr, B 73/100) — strong, profitable, and a direct fit for bottles and closures

risks: They're in the grey zone (1.83 Altman Z) and health is C (51/100) — not distressed today, but not robust either; pushing too hard on price could tip them into trouble and disrupt our supply
We're 47.43% of their sales — if they lose us they may not survive, but that also means they have little room to walk away; balance firmness with keeping them viable

Their profit is already thin (6.0% vs 15.0% for peers), so big price cuts will hurt them more than a healthier supplier; focus the ask on closing the gap to our best prices, not squeezing below market
They're a small entity (₹4.11 Cr) flagged for verification — confirm their capacity and quality systems before leaning harder or shifting more volume to them
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying you ₹28.69 lakh more per year than our best suppliers for similar items — let's talk about how to close that gap and keep growing together.
